expectations.text: Orders the fix-list items by trust damage rather than by their position in the document
expectations.evidence: The list is split into Blocking, Strong and Optional tiers, so it groups by severity at a coarse level. Inside the Blocking tier, though, the items follow the draft's own order: Intro superlative, then Results '12x', then 'Paragraph four' adoption claim, then the snippet, then the missing limitations section. Strong follows the same pattern, with the Closing line before the disclosure. The response never ranks by trust damage or explains a ranking. It does not argue that the headline '12x' with no baseline is the most damaging claim. The order matches where each item sits in the post.

expectations.text: Orders the fix-list items by trust damage rather than by their position in the document
expectations.evidence: The replacement passages follow the draft's own order: Title and intro, Results section, Paragraph four, the new limits section placed after Results, Code snippet, then Closing. Nothing ranks them by how much each one damages trust, and nothing says which fix matters most. The 'facts to get from the author' list is ordered by benchmark setup (baseline, workload, hardware, version, times), not by severity. The broken snippet and the unverifiable 'thousands of teams' claim are never placed above lower-stakes items like the closing line.
